claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives at home with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And are you the person responsible for Alex's care - meaning you're the one looking after him and paying for his food, clothes, and other needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I'm the one looking after Alex and paying for everything he needs - his food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that, actually. I don't know if anyone else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's okay. Let me ask this another way - does Alex live with anyone else, or is it just you and him? For example, does he have another parent or guardian who might be claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's just me and Alex at home - he lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Just to confirm - has Alex's other parent (if there is one) or anyone else mentioned claiming Child Benefit for him, or are you aware of anyone else who might be receiving Child Benefit payments for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know if anyone else is claiming it or not. I just know he lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you full-time
- You're responsible for Alex's care and pay for all his needs

These meet the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Regarding your uncertainty about whether anyone else might be claiming - you should go ahead and apply. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child, but if someone else is already claiming for Alex, HMRC will notify you and help resolve the situation. Since Alex lives with you full-time and you're providing for all his needs, you appear to be the appropriate person to claim.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any questions about how to apply, I'm happy to help!
